record.title: StarVLA-α reports competitive VLA results with a compact Qwen3-VL policy
record.summary: The Sep 16, 2026 v2 of StarVLA-α studies a deliberately simple vision-language-action baseline built from a Qwen3-VL-4B backbone and an MLP action head. Across LIBERO, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, the authors report competitive results for benchmark-specific policies and a single model jointly trained across datasets. On RoboChallenge, the paper reports 33.6% success and 54.5 progress for StarVLA-α on the ARX5 11-task set, versus 12.7% and 27.6 for π0.5. Additional appendices report real-world out-of-distribution tasks and LIBERO-Plus perturbation results. These measurements are paper-reported; independent reproduction, several physical-trial denominators and variability estimates remain open.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The v2 paper specifies StarVLA-α as a compact VLA policy using a Qwen3-VL-4B vision-language backbone and an MLP action head, and describes both per-benchmark specialist training and one jointly trained generalist model.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Authors report competitive specialist and generalist results across LIBERO, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1. Their Table 5 reports the generalist StarVLA-α results alongside specialist systems and baselines; performance is not uniformly best on every benchmark column.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the ARX5 RoboChallenge 11-task set, authors report StarVLA-α at 33.6% success and 54.5 progress, versus π0.5 at 12.7% and 27.6. The paper also reports three physical-robot OOD tasks and LIBERO-Plus perturbation results in appendices.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish independent reproducibility, general superiority of minimal architectures, or transfer to materially different robot/task distributions beyond its stated regimes.

evidence_gaps.description: Reported simulation, RoboChallenge and OOD results have not been independently reproduced; the author-linked code/artifacts were not audited here.
Several physical-robot results and appendix summaries do not expose complete trial denominators or uncertainty estimates in the inspected sections.
The evidence does not establish transfer beyond the named benchmarks and robot setups or matched cost against more complex policies.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported results hold, a compact Qwen3-VL-4B backbone with an MLP action head offers a meaningful VLA design baseline that competes across simulation suites and one physical-robot benchmark without benchmark-specific model architecture. That can change local architecture and evaluation choices, but the evidence is one author-run preprint with limited real-robot and independent-reproduction evidence.
limitations: All capability and benchmark measurements are author-reported; no independent reproduction or artifact audit was performed.
The reported generalist comparison covers four named benchmark families and uses the paper's data and training pipeline; it is not a universal comparison across VLA stacks.
The RoboChallenge result cited in the abstract is for an ARX5 11-task set; other appendix results use distinct platforms, tasks and settings.
Physical-robot trial counts and statistical uncertainty are incomplete in the inspected summaries; no deployment-level reliability or safety conclusion follows.
The paper's architectural simplicity does not establish that added components are unnecessary in other data, embodiment or control regimes.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report competitive benchmark results for a compact Qwen3-VL-4B/MLP-action policy and one jointly trained generalist across LIBERO, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1. On the ARX5 RoboChallenge 11-task set, they report 33.6% success and 54.5 progress versus π0.5 at 12.7% and 27.6.
technical.demonstrated_result: The v2 preprint documents the architecture and evaluation protocols, including specialist versus generalist settings, a RoboChallenge physical-robot evaluation, real-world OOD tasks and LIBERO-Plus perturbations. The numerical results remain author-reported and were not reproduced by the research desk.
technical.mechanism: Initialize a Qwen3-VL-4B vision-language backbone and train a compact MLP action head under a standardized VLA pipeline. The authors compare benchmark-specific policies with one model jointly trained across datasets and examine action modeling, robot-specific pretraining and interface choices.
technical.regime: Paper-reported evaluation on LIBERO, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1; physical-robot RoboChallenge results include an ARX5 set of 11 tasks. Appendices add three real-world OOD tasks and LIBERO-Plus perturbations. Results use author-selected datasets, training protocols and baselines.
technical.strongest_baseline: In Table 5, the generalist StarVLA-α is compared with per-benchmark specialist systems including π0.5, GR00T-N1.6 and specialist StarVLA-α variants. The ARX5 RoboChallenge comparison reports π0.5 at 12.7% success / 27.6 progress against StarVLA-α at 33.6% / 54.5; these are author-run matched task-set results, not independent cross-lab measurements.

brief.title: StarVLA-α reports competitive VLA results with a compact Qwen3-VL policy
brief.why_it_matters: Vision-language-action results often entangle architecture changes with data pipelines, embodiment setup and benchmark-specific engineering. A simple, openly described baseline with cross-benchmark and physical-robot results can help researchers compare those choices and determine when extra architecture is useful. The paper does not establish that simpler policies generally win or that its reported gains transfer beyond the named tasks and setups.
